as_told.title: Townsend Brown at the Institute of Field Physics, Wright Field sponsorship
as_told.place_text: Institute of Field Physics, North Carolina

plain: The physicist Bryce DeWitt, who helped found quantum gravity, a field that later led to string theory, ran the Institute of Field Physics in North Carolina, and at the same time it was paying for the high-voltage gravity experiments of the researcher Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels tells this himself in three episodes, without naming a source. In other versions he says Wright Field, a military air base, sponsored a 1957 meeting of top physicists at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill while the university backed Brown's anti-gravity work, and in one he names the Air Force general Curtis LeMay as a sponsor, calls the institute a CIA outpost studying anti-gravity, and mentions a video of a champagne celebration there. If true, mainstream physics and secret anti-gravity research would have been funded side by side.
